6. Review the draft in [Releases](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases), and publish it.

### Release notes

Write the notes for users. Copy this structure:

```markdown
### Added
- **Short summary in bold** (#33, added in #44). What changed, for whom, and what to do, in a few sentences. See [Doc title](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/vX.Y.Z/docs/file.md#anchor).

### Fixed
- **Short summary in bold** (#42, fixed in #43). ...
```

- Use the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) headings, in this order: `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`, `Security`. Write only the headings that have items.
- Write one item for each change that users can see. Do not write items for CI, refactoring, or tests.
- After the summary, write the issue and the pull request, such as `(#42, fixed in #43)`. If there is no issue, write only the pull request, such as `(#43)`.
- Use full links to the docs of the tag (`blob/vX.Y.Z/...`), so that the links stay correct after later releases.
- Do not add the **Full Changelog** link. `release.yml` adds it.

## Pull requests

1. Make a branch with a descriptive name, such as `feat/123-description`.
2. Write tests for new behavior.
3. Make sure that all hooks and `npm run check` pass.
4. Use Conventional Commits.
5. Keep the change small: one feature or one fix in each pull request.
6. Update the documentation when you add features or change behavior.

## Questions

---
|-------|--------|
| `exclude_tools` | pi-action disables these tools completely. Neither the model nor other tools can call them |
| `model_tools_hidden` | pi-action does not offer these tools to the model. Other tools can still call them, for example pit's `tools.*` |

pit 0.36.0 and later hide the coding tools from the model themselves. The model gets only pit's `typescript` tool without these inputs, and pit's programs use `workspace.*` and `shell.*` instead of the coding tools (see [Tools the model sees](https://github.com/cv/pit/blob/main/docs/durable.md#tools-the-model-sees) in pit). With an earlier pit, hide the coding tools with `model_tools_hidden`. Its programs can then still call them through `tools.*`:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    extensions: |
      github:cv/pit#v0.35.1
    model_tools_hidden: read, write, edit, bash
```

- Write one name per line, or separate names with commas. `*` matches any characters, as in pit's `allowedTools`. For example, `mcp_*`.
- pi-action resolves the names against the tools after it installs the extensions, and after the [overrides](#override-tools-and-sections). For a name that matches no tool, pi-action writes a warning.
- If the inputs leave the model with no tools, the run fails.
- pi-action applies the inputs on each run. When an input is empty, pi-action clears the setting of an earlier run on the thread.
- The `🤖` line of the log shows the tools that the model gets, for example `🤖 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · thinking medium · tools: typescript · extensions: pit (typescript)`.
